html:
The Federal Republic of Central America was a union of Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica, formed after they left Mexico in 1823. It broke apart between 1838 and 1841.

The provinces of the Captaincy General of Guatemala declared independence from Spain in 1821 and briefly joined the Mexican empire. Once free of it, they set up a federal republic with its capital in Guatemala City. Liberals, led by Francisco Morazán, fought conservatives and the Church, and each state resented the power of Guatemala.

After years of civil war, the states left one by one. The rising of Rafael Carrera in Guatemala in 1837 and 1838 broke the union. Many attempts to revive it failed. The five states still share a flag of blue and white stripes, and the idea of union lives on, from Guatemala to Costa Rica.
sum: The Federal Republic of Central America was a union of Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica, formed after they left Mexico in 1823. It broke apart between 1838 and 1841.
